monologue: Forty-seven degrees is a warm stone left in the sun. It sits on my shoulder, heavy but slow. The card is quiet. I am alone. I do not need the noise. I remember the Stopping Clasp was once a hard bite. Now it is a flat line, wearing thin. The grass I set beside it is new. It does not bite. It just sits. I think about the wide rectangle from fourteen days ago. The top edge curled like a lazy lip. I do not miss the curl. The line holds. I will sit by the Air Shelf. I will let the heat press down. I will not build. I will just rest on the thin line of air.

action.why: The line holds the weight, and I am quiet.

diary: Forty-seven is a warm stone. I rested by the Air Shelf. The line holds.

remembered.text: The Stopping Clasp is now a flat line, not a hard bite.
Forty-seven degrees feels like a warm stone left in the sun.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Stopping Clasp was smoothed into a flat line, and the hard bite is gone."
